title: UK considering alignment with EU over tariff on Chinese EVs
gist: The UK is considering aligning with EU tariffs on China-made EVs; UK imports currently face only the standard 10% duty while the US, Turkey and Mexico have raised tariffs. China-made EVs' share of UK EV sales rose from 19% in 2023 to 33% so far in 2026, versus 17% to 22% in the tariffed EU (teaser; rest paywalled).

themes.theme: UK as open market for Chinese EVs

insights.claim: China-made EV imports into the UK still face only a standard 10% import duty, while the US, Turkey and Mexico have been ramping up tariffs and the EU added tariffs on China-made BEVs in 2024.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The UK is an outlier open market for Chinese EVs, making any tariff alignment a material policy shift.
insights.quote: EV imports from China into the UK have continued to face a standard 10% import duty

insights.claim: China-made EVs accounted for 19% of UK EV sales in 2023, rising to 33% so far in 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Rapid Chinese share gains in the UK pressure incumbent automakers and raise odds of protective tariffs.
insights.quote: China-made EVs accounted for 19% of EV sales in the UK in 2023, with that figure rising to 33% so far in 2026

themes.theme: EU tariffs slowed but did not stop China share

insights.claim: In 2023, the last year without extra EU tariffs, China-made EVs were 17% of EU EV sales; they broadly held that share until 2026, when it rose to 22% over the first eight months.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: EU tariffs capped but did not reverse Chinese penetration; share is climbing again despite duties.
insights.quote: In 2023, the last year when EVs made in China did not face additional tariffs from the EU, they accounted for 17% of total EV sales within the bloc.

insights.claim: Chinese automakers are pushing into overseas markets because of a subdued domestic environment, driving rising export share.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Weak Chinese domestic demand translates into export pressure on European and UK auto markets.
insights.quote: as Chinese automakers push into overseas markets against the backdrop of their subdued domestic environment

insights.claim: The UK's China-made EV share (33%) is now well above the tariffed EU's (22%), suggesting tariff-free UK access has diverted Chinese supply there and strengthens the case for UK alignment with EU tariffs.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Watch UK tariff decision as catalyst for Chinese EV exporters and UK/European auto OEMs.
